newsitem.title: USA: NYC says water authority deals delayed until Sept.
newsitem.headline: NYC says water authority deals delayed until Sept.

text.p: New York City announced that it has rescheduled four bonds deals, postponing two until early September and slating two for the week of August 5.

The deals involve two offerings by the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority and two deals being done by the New York State Environmental Facilities Authority on behalf of New York City, Water Authority Treasurer Alan Anders said.
"The EFC financings need to be approved by the (New York) State Public Authorities Control Board, and they have approved one of the financings but not the other," he said.

Under the new schedule, New York Municipal Water Finance Authority will sell $300 million of refunding bonds on August 5, he said. Previously the deal had been announced as $150 million for the same date. A retail order period is set to begin Friday, August 1.

Also on August 5, the New York State Environmental Facilities Corp will sell $115 million new money financing for New York Water, Anders said. The $115 million was the same amount EFC announced previously.
As for the other two deals, EFC had earlier announced a $450 million to $700 million refunding for New York water, while the Water Authority had announced $400 million new money offering.

"They are both going to come the week of September 15," Anders said. "They had previously announced to come at the same time as the first two. Because the EFC refunding did not get Public Authority Control Board approval, New York Water does not require approval but we are doing the Water new money in conjunction with the EFC refunding."
